Aa

Macrons

Consonantal i

Consonantal u

Theme

Money, work & business

investment noun

also invest, invest money, investments, a good investment, investor, investors

classical

Cic. Imp. Pomp. 18: in eā prōvinciā pecūniās magnās conlocātās habent

pecūnia collocāta

noun and participle

money invested, an investment

Latin says it with the verb: pecūniam collocāre, to invest money; to invest in a farm, in fundō collocāre (Cic. Caecin. 11, Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • collocō, collocāre, collocāvī, collocātum — invest (money)

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 2.87: dē quaerendā, dē collocandā pecūniā; Cic. Caecin. 15: nusquam posse eam melius conlocārī; Traupman 334 · Conjugation on Wiktionary

    Also spelled conlocō.

  • pecūniae collocātiō — investment

    noun and genitive · also used · modern · Traupman 334

    Traupman’s noun; classically collocātiō is a placing or arrangement, or the giving of a daughter in marriage (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • dē quaerendā, dē collocandā pecūniā (vellem etiam dē ūtendā)

    on how to make money and how to invest it (I wish also on how to use it)Cic. Off. 2.87

  • nusquam posse eam melius conlocārī

    it could not be better invested anywhereCic. Caecin. 15

See also fund, interest, profit, bank.
